chunks: 3951 - Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is it permissible to enter into a salam contract for food with a man who has neither food nor livestock with him, except that when the appointed term comes, he buys it and delivers it in full?” He said: “If he guarantees it until a specified term, then there is no harm in it.”
He said: I said, “What do you think—if he delivers part of it to me and delays part of it, is that permissible?” He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أَوْفَانِي: delivered to me in full or fulfilled for me
key_terms.الْأَجَلُ: the due date or appointed term for delivery
key_terms.حَيَوَانٌ: livestock or animal goods mentioned as sale items
key_terms.ضَمِنَهُ: guaranteed it as an enforceable obligation
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal objection or harm in it
key_terms.يُسْلِمَ: to enter into a salam contract through advance payment

ai.seo_question: Is a salam sale valid if the seller does not yet own the goods but promises to buy and deliver them later?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on salam transactions, allowing advance payment for food even when the seller does not presently possess the goods, so long as he guarantees delivery by a specified term. It also permits partial fulfillment with delay of the remainder. The narration is significant for Shia fiqh discussions on deferred delivery, contractual liability, and lawful commercial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3951 - Al-Nadr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as): "Is it permissible to enter into a Salam contract for food with a man who does not currently possess the food or livestock, but promises to purchase it and deliver it when the due date arrives?"
Imam (as) replied: "If he guarantees it for a specified term, then there is no harm in it."

I then asked: "What if he delivers part of it and delays the rest? Is that permissible?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes."
